Join the leading maritime news network ImagineStock / Shutterstock Spain will ban wastewater discharges from ship exhaust gas cleaning systems, commonly known as scrubbers, in its ports and internal waters beginning July 1, 2027, imposing restrictions that go beyond existing regional environmental requirements. The measure, established under Royal Decree 1006/2026 and published November 20, applies to all civilian vessels regardless of flag. It covers discharges from open-loop, closed-loop and hybrid scrubber systems in Spanish internal waters, port areas and designated anchorages. Scrubbers allow ships to meet International Maritime Organization (IMO) sulfur emissions limits while continuing to burn higher-sulfur fuel oil. However, the systems can generate wastewater containing heavy metals, hydrocarbons and other pollutants. The new rules implement a 2025 decision by the OSPAR Commission, which oversees marine environmental protection in the Northeast Atlantic. That agreement requires participating countries to prohibit open-loop scrubber discharges in ports and internal waters by July 2027, with restrictions extending to all scrubber operating modes by July 2029. Spain has chosen to accelerate the broader prohibition by two years and extend it nationwide, including to Mediterranean ports outside the OSPAR region. The ban does not prohibit scrubber use or apply across all Spanish territorial waters. Instead, vessels must stop discharging wastewater before entering restricted areas, either switching to compliant low-sulfur fuel or retaining wastewater onboard where technically possible. Spain already restricts scrubber discharges at several major ports, including Algeciras, Barcelona, Cartagena and Valencia. The decree establishes a common national standard. Spanish shipowners’ association ANAVE has criticized the accelerated timetable and broader geographic scope, calling for greater alignment with IMO guidelines. In its statement, ANAVE questioned whether Spain had adequately justified the additional restrictions through environmental risk assessments. It also raised concerns about the availability of port reception facilities for wastewater from closed-loop systems. The association noted that shipowners have invested heavily in scrubber technology under existing international regulations and warned against measures that undermine regulatory certainty. The decree also introduces reporting and inspection requirements. Scrubber-equipped ships must notify Spanish authorities of their systems at least 24 hours before arrival, or upon departure from the previous port for shorter voyages. Authorities may inspect fuel-changeover records and scrubber operating logs. Spain’s move reflects growing pressure to restrict scrubber wastewater discharges even as the technology remains an accepted method of meeting IMO air pollution standards. U.S. Central Command/Handout via REUTERS The U.S. Treasury Department on Monday announced new sanctions targeting financial networks supporting Iran’s oil exports and tanker operations, including companies accused of facilitating payments for the National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC) and shipping arrangements linked to the Iranian military. The latest action , announced under Operation Economic Outcast, targets 22 entities and eight individuals involved in moving billions of dollars through Iran’s international financial networks. Unlike previous sanctions rounds focused on tankers and shipping companies, the latest measures target the financial infrastructure that allows Iran to collect oil revenues and pay for maritime services despite U.S. restrictions. Among those designated is Dubai-based OGA Global General Trading LLC, which Treasury said facilitated millions of dollars in payments for NITC, Iran’s state-owned tanker operator. Treasury also identified a tanker chartering arrangement involving the SERENE I (IMO 9197832). According to the department, Dubai-based H N B Trading Co LLC facilitated payment for the vessel’s charter involving Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company, an Iranian military-linked entity, and sanctioned shipping company Dragon Road Ltd. Other targets include Dubai-based Gespl International General Trading LLC, accused of facilitating oil and petrochemical sales for the National Iranian Oil Company, and Integral Petro Energy Trading LLC, which allegedly facilitated millions of dollars in liquefied petroleum gas sales involving Kharg Petrochemical Company. The sanctions also target the Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold, which Treasury described as a central mechanism for connecting Iranian exporters earning foreign currency with importers seeking funds for overseas purchases. The institution reportedly supports tens of billions of dollars in annual trade, including transactions using Chinese yuan and Russian rubles. The action comes just days after Treasury claimed that no Iranian oil had been loaded onto vessels since Operation Economic Outcast began on August 24 and that no Iranian oil remained afloat outside the U.S. military blockade. Under U.S. sanctions rules, assets belonging to designated entities within U.S. jurisdiction are blocked, while foreign financial institutions may face additional sanctions exposure for facilitating certain transactions involving those entities. articles.body: Maersk will reduce its Peak Season Surcharge (PSS) for dry container shipments from the Indian Subcontinent to the US and Canadian East and Gulf coasts. The revised charges will apply from 24 November 2026 to non-SPOT bookings. For shipments from Nhava Sheva, Mundra, Pipavav, Hazira, Nepal and Bhutan to covered ports other than Houston, the surcharge will be US$2,650 for a 20-foot dry container and US$2,950 for 40-foot dry, 40-foot high-cube and 45-foot high-cube equipment. Cargo originating in South and East India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and the Maldives will face a surcharge of US$3,100 per container to covered destinations other than Houston. Maersk will apply a separate US$4,800 surcharge to shipments from India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Nepal and Bhutan bound for Houston. articles.body: Russian Wheat Export Prices Spike After Trilateral Summit Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © Adobe Stock/MaxSafaniuk Russian wheat ex port prices spiked last week following the trilateral summit of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen, analysts said. Ex port prices for wheat with 12.5% protein content shipped from Vysotsk and Ust-Luga were at $246 a metric ton free on board for delivery in late December–early January by the end of last week, up $3 from the previous week, consultancy IKAR said "It was a short-term surge in demand linked to the aftermath of the (trilateral) summit in China," said Dmitry Rylko, head of IKAR As expected, the Trump–Putin–Xi meeting produced no progress on Ukraine, which was not mentioned in the joint statement, Andrei Sizov, head of the Sovecon, said Ukraine carried out several strikes on the Kerch Bridge last week. One of its two arches collapsed, blocking the Kerch–Yenikale Canal, the only shipping route between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov Reopening the canal will require clearing the debris, which is expected to take at least several weeks, Sizov said Putin said on Thursday that Moscow would no longer consider a moratorium on strikes in the Black Sea or on energy infrastructure following Ukraine's attacks on the bridge linking Russia and Crimea, vowing a harsh response Ex port s to the Baltic Sea are picking up pace. According to Russian Railways, port s in Russia's northwest have increased their transshipment capacity to 32 million metric tons from 8.6 million tons. The river transit of grain for ex port has been sup port ed by the possibility of extending the navigation season, particularly along the Volga-Baltic Waterway IKAR estimated that wheat ex port s in November could fall to between 2.7 million tons and 2.9 million tons from 3.1 million tons in October. SovEcon maintains its ex port forecast for November at 2.7 million tons, down from 2.9 million tons in October Rusagrotrans estimates wheat ex port s in November at between 2.9 million tons and 3.1 million metric tons, compared with 3.15 million tons a week earlier Russia has nearly completed the 2026 grain harvest. articles.title: Oil Prices Fall As Middle East Flows Increase
articles.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday as a rise in supplies from the Middle East and the restart of a Libyan oil pipeline offset unease about persistent shipping and refinery attacks in the region.Brent crude futures fell $2.02, or 2.18%, to $90.55 a barrel by 1436 GMT.
articles.body: Oil Prices Fall As Middle East Flows Increase Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © Adobe Stock/le Oil prices fell on Monday as a rise in supplies from the Middle East and the restart of a Libyan oil pipeline offset unease about persistent shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent crude futures fell $2.02, or 2.18%, to $90.55 a barrel by 1436 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures were down $1.59, or 1.91%, at $81.82 a barrel. Earlier in the session, both contracts fell by more than 3%, with Brent hitting its lowest level in two weeks at $89.48 a barrel while WTI fell to its lowest since August 27 at $80.55. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened and crude is beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the chairman of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Monday. Meanwhile, JPMorgan expects oil futures to fall to the high $70s in the first half of 2027 due to an estimated supply surplus, with higher Middle East production outside Iran next year along with more supply from the Americas led by the US. Bank of America said geopolitics would remain the key driver of oil prices, with relatively low global inventories leaving much of the world vulnerable to supply disruptions. "It is partly the growing signs of a glut, but with each passing day it seems less likely that Trump will attack again," said IG chief market analyst Chris Beauchamp. On Sunday, however, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement said it attacked a Saudi Arabian oil refinery, while the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported multiple attacks on shipping in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in the kingdom, home to the US Navy's 5th Fleet. "It would be irresponsible to conclude that oil will now be supplied uninterruptedly and in vast volumes. Iranian attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz are taking their toll," said PVM analyst Tamas Varga. In Turkey, talks on Sunday at the global climate conference COP31 collapsed for the first time since 2009 after nations could not agree on a deal on including a statement on the phase-out of fossil fuels. Saudi Arabia and other big oil-producing countries have said fossil fuels will play a role in the economy for the foreseeable future and they lobbied to keep any mention of fossil fuels out of the text, observers at the conference said. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their 2027 output policy. The group is made up of OPEC and other oil producers such as Russia. (Reuters)

articles.title: Russia to Spend $576m on Kaliningrad Supply Ferries
articles.summary: Russia will spend 47 billion roubles ($576 million) to build two giant rail ferries to ensure uninterrupted supplies to its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad amid rising tensions in the region, Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said on Monday.Kaliningrad…
articles.body: Russia to Spend $576m on Kaliningrad Supply Ferries Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © andriano_cz - stock.adobe.com Russia will spend 47 billion roubles ($576 million) to build two giant rail ferries to ensure uninterrupted supplies to its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad amid rising tensions in the region, Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said on Monday. Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave located between EU and NATO members Poland and Lithuania, has become increasingly reliant on the sea route since 2022, after Lithuania banned transit of many goods, including construction materials, through its territory in compliance with the EU sanctions against Russia. "Kaliningrad region has a special geography, and due to the unlawful actions of certain countries, disruptions to logistics chains and attempts at a transport blockade are complicating the operations of enterprises located there," Mishustin said. The two ferries are expected to go into operation in 2030 and operate between the port of Ust-Luga in Russia's Leningrad region and Baltiysk in Kaliningrad. Most of the money will come from Russia's rainy-day fund, Mishustin said. The announcement comes after Sparta II, a Russian cargo ship with links to the military that transported cargo to Kaliningrad, was hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday, in what Finland's military said was likely an attack by Ukraine, highlighting growing security risks in the region. Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said on November 21 that a drone alert went off in a district bordering Lithuania after an appearance of a "suspicious object." In a document sent to NATO in September, Russia warned NATO it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if the Western alliance attempted to cut off Kaliningrad. Maritime shipping now accounts for over half of supplies to Kaliningrad, compared with just 8% in 2021, before the war in Ukraine started. About 30 ships, including four rail ferries, now transport goods between the exclave and Russian ports on the Baltic Sea. ($1 = 81.5841 roubles) (Reuters)

articles.title: At the Helm of Change: Athens to Host Critical Maritime Industry Conversations in 2027

articles.body: At the Helm of Change: Athens to Host Critical Maritime Industry Conversations in 2027 in Hellenic Shipping News 23/11/2026 The future of shipping is being shaped by decisions made today. From the growing complexity of environmental regulations to the rapid advancement of maritime technology, the industry faces a period of transformation that demands more than theoretical solutions. On May 25-26, 2027, Athens will provide a meeting point for the people navigating these changes at the Greek Maritime Forum 2027. Hosted by Marensia Group, the forum will gather more than 800 maritime professionals, including shipowners, ship managers, technology providers, policymakers, and industry specialists, for two days of discussion, knowledge exchange, and business networking. With over 60 speakers, 12 panel discussions, and an exhibition featuring more than 50 companies, the event aims to bridge the gap between emerging industry ambitions and the commercial realities of operating in today’s shipping environment. The Greek Shipping Community at the Centre of Global Dialogue Greece has long held a prominent position in international shipping, with Greek shipowners playing a significant role in global seaborne trade. As the maritime industry confronts new regulatory frameworks, changing energy requirements, and technological disruption, the experience and perspectives of the Greek shipping community remain particularly relevant. The Greek Maritime Forum 2027 will build on this position, bringing international industry stakeholders to Athens to exchange practical insights and examine how shipping businesses can respond to an increasingly demanding operating environment. Rather than focusing solely on emerging trends, the programme will address the decisions, investments, and operational adjustments required to turn industry developments into workable solutions. The Cost of Change: Regulations, Fuels and Infrastructure For shipowners and operators, the transition towards lower-emission shipping raises fundamental questions about cost, feasibility, and long-term planning. How can companies prepare for evolving environmental requirements while protecting operational efficiency? Which alternative fuel pathways offer realistic opportunities? And how quickly can maritime infrastructure adapt to support the transition? These questions will form part of the forum’s sustainability discussions, including Decarbonization Rules & Reality, The Alternative Fuels Reality Check, and Decarbonizing Ports & Harbors. The sessions will explore the practical implications of regulatory developments, the commercial challenges associated with alternative marine fuels, and the infrastructure requirements facing ports and harbours. With the maritime energy transition affecting decisions across vessel ownership, fleet management, and port operations, the discussions will provide an opportunity to examine different approaches to one of shipping’s most significant long-term challenges. Beyond Digitalisation: What Technology Actually Delivers The shipping industry has no shortage of technological solutions. The more pressing question is how effectively these innovations can be integrated into everyday operations. At the Greek Maritime Forum 2027, digital transformation will be examined through the lens of practical application and operational value. Panels including The AI-Enabled Fleet, Maritime Digital Transformation, and Cybersecurity in a Connected Maritime World will explore how shipping companies can make better use of data, strengthen digital security, and incorporate emerging technologies into fleet management. The discussions will also consider the growing importance of cybersecurity as maritime operations become increasingly interconnected. For shipowners and managers evaluating new technologies, the focus will be on understanding both the opportunities and the challenges of implementing digital solutions in a complex operational environment. Shipping’s Most Important Asset Remains Its People While technological advancement and environmental regulation dominate much of the maritime conversation, the future of the industry also depends on its workforce. Changing vessel technologies, evolving operational requirements, and growing expectations around seafarer welfare are creating new responsibilities for shipping companies. The forum will address these issues through Crew Wellbeing & Engagement and Crew Skills for the Next Fleet, examining how maritime employers can support their crews and prepare professionals for the demands of modern shipping. The sessions will provide a platform for discussing workforce development, engagement, and the skills required as the industry continues to evolve. Where Industry Conversations Become Business Opportunities The Greek Maritime Forum 2027 will extend beyond its conference sessions, offering participants opportunities to connect directly with companies and decision-makers from across the maritime value chain. More than 50 exhibitors are expected to present technologies, equipment, and services supporting shipping operations, creating opportunities for shipowners and ship managers to discover solutions relevant to their businesses. Dedicated networking sessions and a cocktail reception will offer additional opportunities to establish commercial relationships, exchange perspectives, and explore potential partnerships. By bringing together shipping companies, suppliers, service providers, and technology developers in one setting, the event aims to encourage collaboration across different areas of the industry. Two Days in Athens, Conversations with Global Relevance As international shipping adapts to a changing regulatory, technological, and commercial landscape, opportunities for direct engagement between industry stakeholders remain essential. The Greek Maritime Forum 2027 seeks to provide that environment, combining practical industry discussions with opportunities for business development and professional exchange. For the Greek shipping community and its international partners, the event will offer a chance to examine the challenges ahead, share operational experience, and strengthen the relationships that support global maritime trade. On May 25–26, 2027, Athens will once again provide a stage for conversations that extend far beyond Greek waters. For programme updates, participation opportunities, and further information, visit https://greekmaritimeforum.com/ . articles.body: Maritime Professionals Raise Over US$80,000 for Seafarers in Inaugural Hong Kong Hike in International Shipping News 23/11/2026 Seafarers quite literally keep the global maritime industry afloat, and so it was fitting that the 10th annual Hong Kong Maritime Week began with a major new fundraiser for seafarer welfare. On the morning of Sunday 15 November, nearly 100 shipping professionals from around the world gathered at Hong Kong’s Big Wave Bay for the inaugural Bay to Bay Maritime Hike, tackling a demanding 21-kilometre route through Shek O and Tai Tam Country Parks to the finish line at Repulse Bay. participants gather on the beach at Big Wave Bay Organised by The Mission to Seafarers Hong Kong alongside industry co-organisers The Captain’s Table, NorthStandard, and Filhet-Allard Maritime Hong Kong, the challenge attracted teams from more than 20 maritime companies and institutions, including ship managers, marine insurers, shipping agents, and educational bodies. Together, participants raised over US$80,000 to support the international work of the Mission to Seafarers, which operates in more than 200 ports across 50 countries. The charity provides emergency assistance, practical support, and a warm welcome for crew members far from home. Sunday’s race was won by a team from ship management company Anglo-Eastern, comprising CIO Torbjorn Dimblad alongside Lucas Daels and Timo De Koning. The Belgian-Scandinavian trio, who dubbed themselves the ‘Anglo-Eastern Waffle Vikings’, strode home in two hours and forty eight minutes, some forty minutes ahead of the nearest competition. the race gets underway The silver and bronze medal positions were taken by GARDians on the Run, entered by marine insurer Gard, and WK Venture from shipping company Wah Kwong, whose line-up included the first female finishers, Abbie Hui and Jieying Peng. Teams from Fratelli Cosulich and The Caravel Group rounded out the top five, while the all-female Sirens of the Steep deserve special recognition for having one of the day’s more inventive team names. This event is a powerful expression of that support, and we are deeply grateful to everyone who helped make it possible.” Chris Hall, the managing director of the American P&I Club in Hong Kong, was among the participants in the race. The route across Dragon’s Back, a mountain ridge in the south-east of Hong Kong Island, “has some of the best views in Hong Kong”, he said. “You’d be hard-pressed to come up with a more classic Hong Kong hike”. “Out on the course there was an overwhelming sense of comaraderie,” Hall said. “We were jumping ahead and behind the same two or three teams for much of the race, and it was all good fun. Many of us in the shipping industry are not dealing day to day with seafarers, but events like this are a way that we can support them, and show how much we value them.” Source: Mission to Seafarers Hong Kong 2026-11-23 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.summary: Arc, a marine technology company, announced it has been selected to provide the power management and electrical systems for USX-1 Defiant, the unmanned surface vessel developed under the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's (DARPA) No Manning Required Ship (NOMARS) program.
articles.body: Arc to Supply Power Management, Electrical Systems for USV Defiant Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 The NOMARS program’s demonstration vessel, USX-1 Defiant, completed construction in February 2025. Source: DARPA | Colie Wertz Arc, a marine technology company, announced it has been selected to provide the power management and electrical systems for USX-1 Defiant , the unmanned surface vessel developed under the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's (DARPA) No Manning Required Ship (NOMARS) program. Under the funded agreement, Arc Boats will integrate the vessel's high-voltage power management hardware and software, bringing the company's commercial electrification expertise into an autonomous maritime program. Defiant is a technology demonstrator designed to prove that a ship can operate reliably without a crew. The vessel has no berthing, galley, or life-support systems on board, allowing it to remain at sea, fully unmanned, for up to 90 days. Arc Boats is developing and integrating the vessel's electrical backbone—a fault-tolerant, self-healing DC-power system that autonomously monitors diagnostic information and can resolve without human intervention. Arc Boats’ architecture also enables remote startup of high-voltage systems, a process that once required a technician. For a vessel operating unmanned for months at sea, autonomy is the difference between a mission that succeeds and one that ends early. Arc Boats’ experience translates directly to the reliability and redundancy demands of unmanned maritime platforms. As part of the agreement, the company will advise DARPA throughout system integration, helping shape an electrical architecture designed to support future defense applications. The defense sector is increasingly investing in crewless maritime platforms across a range of programs. These programs share a common need for more capable powertrains—ones that deliver extended range, greater reliability, and software-defined control. Moving from mechanical to electrical architectures like the ones developed by Arc Boats delivers those improved capabilities. As adoption of unmanned platforms accelerates, dependable power infrastructure won't just support long-duration, crewless missions, it will determine whether the mission is possible at all. Arc Boats’ work on Defiant marks another step in bringing its advanced integrated power systems into critical defense applications.

articles.title: Iranian Floating Crude Storage Drops to Under 4 Million Barrels
articles.summary: Iran’s floating crude storage in Asia is nearly gone. Windward put Iranian crude stored on tankers off Malaysia at about 70 million barrels in January, and at most about 3.8 million barrels remain. The tankers that delivered that crude are sitting empty off Sri Lanka.
articles.body: Iranian Floating Crude Storage Drops to Under 4 Million Barrels Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 Iranian floating storage at the Singapore/Malaysia EOPL anchorage, January to November 20, 2026. Source: Windward Iran’s floating crude storage in Asia is nearly gone. Windward put Iranian crude stored on tankers off Malaysia at about 70 million barrels in January, and at most about 3.8 million barrels remain. The tankers that delivered that crude are sitting empty off Sri Lanka. As the stock in Asia runs out, a larger Iranian attempt to move crude past the U.S. blockade becomes more likely. Iran’s crude buffer in Asia sits on tankers at Malaysia’s Eastern Outer Port Limits (EOPL) anchorage. After Windward's January prediction, it was about 30 million barrels in late March. On 12 July, Windward tracked nine sanctioned Iranian tankers at EOPL with AIS off, holding about 14.6 million barrels. As of November 20, only two Iran-linked VLCCs at the anchorage were last reported laden: M.T HEDY (IMO 9212888) on June 19 and FIONA II (IMO 9262766) on September 11. Together they hold at most about 3.8 million barrels. The tankers that carried that crude have not gone back to Iran for more. On August 30, Windward flagged 21 Iran-flagged ships drifting off Sri Lanka, 20 of them empty crude tankers. Nearly three months later they are still there. On November 20, 20 sanctioned tankers, 18 of them VLCCs, were at ballast draught off Sri Lanka, which indicates they are empty. Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from the same day shows a tanker at 19 of their 20 AIS positions. That is about 38 million barrels of empty capacity waiting for the U.S. blockade to open. The pressure on Iran to move crude is building. The first attempt to cross the blockade line will likely come from tankers that are already loaded and close. Four laden crude tankers carrying an estimated 4.9 million barrels are between the Strait of Hormuz and the line, within about a day’s sailing of it. As the stock in Asia runs out, a larger crude push becomes more likely. Sanctioned VLCCs at the EOPL anchorage on satellite imagery. Only M.T HEDY and FIONA II last reported laden. Wood, who founded BHGI in 1995 and later established TSGI in 2010, the transition represents the continuation of a vision that began more than three decades ago. The transition to employee ownership is a step in securing that future, ensuring that the companies they founded continue to grow and succeed for generations to come. Gregory and Cory will remain at the forefront of both companies, providing leadership and direction alongside their established management teams. Clients can continue to expect the same level of service and technical expertise from the employees they've come to know and trust over the years. The engineering teams will continue under the direction of Daniel at BHGI and Harrison at TSGI, both as Engineering Managers. BHGI's History BHGI traces its origins back to 1993, when Gregory and Cory, along with Andy Tyska of Bristol Marine and another fellow student at the University of Michigan Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Department, set out to design a passenger vessel while still in school. REUTERS/Alessandro Bianchi Francesco Schettino, the former captain of the Costa Concordia cruise ship that capsized off Italy in 2012, killing 32 people, has been released from prison after more than nine years behind bars. Schettino, 66, left Rome’s Rebibbia prison Friday evening after a supervisory court approved his request to serve the remainder of his sentence under the supervision of social services, according to Italian news agency ANSA. The decision follows a review of his conduct and participation in rehabilitation programs during his imprisonment. Schettino was sentenced to 16 years and one month for his role in the January 13, 2012, disaster, when the Costa Concordia struck rocks near the Italian island of Giglio during an unauthorized close-to-shore maneuver. The collision opened a massive gash in the vessel’s hull, causing flooding and a loss of power. The ship eventually capsized near the island, triggering a chaotic nighttime evacuation of more than 4,200 passengers and crew. Schettino became the focus of international outrage after leaving the vessel before the evacuation was complete. Investigators also identified delays in ordering passengers to abandon ship. He was convicted of multiple manslaughter, causing a shipwreck and abandoning ship. Italy’s highest court upheld his prison sentence in May 2017 , prompting his immediate imprisonment. Under the newly approved arrangement, Schettino will live in southern Italy’s Campania region, where he is expected to work eight hours a day in an administrative position with a private employer. He must also perform weekly volunteer work and comply with restrictions on his movements, including remaining at home overnight. According to ANSA, good-conduct credits have also advanced his projected sentence completion date to July 2030, approximately two years earlier than previously expected. The Costa Concordia disaster remains one of the deadliest cruise ship accidents in modern history. The wreck was righted in 2013 and refloated in 2014 before being towed to Genoa for dismantling, ending one of the most complex salvage operations ever undertaken. Schettino’s release comes less than two months before the 15th anniversary of the disaster. Finnish Border Guard/Handout via REUTERS The Russian cargo ship Sparta II , severely damaged in a suspected Ukrainian drone attack in the Gulf of Finland, has been towed out of Finnish waters following a multinational firefighting operation, Finnish President Alexander Stubb confirmed. The departure came despite a temporary sanctions-related restriction imposed by Finnish authorities after determining that the vessel belonged to a company subject to European Union sanctions. “The Russian vessel, Sparta II, has now left Finnish territorial waters. In its current state it posed a serious danger in the Gulf of Finland,” Stubb said in a statement Sunday. “Unfortunately, the consequences of Russia’s war of aggression are also visible in our region,” he added, thanking Finnish authorities for their handling of the incident. The Russian-flagged cargo ship was struck by drones Saturday while sailing through international waters west of Russia’s Gogland Island, en route from St. Petersburg to Kaliningrad. The attack sparked a fire aboard the 121-meter vessel, which subsequently lost maneuverability and drifted into Finnish territorial waters near Loviisa. All 16 crew members were evacuated onto another Russian vessel. One reportedly suffered minor injuries. Finnish defense officials have assessed that Ukraine was likely responsible for the attack, although Kyiv has not publicly claimed responsibility. In a statement Monday , Finland’s National Enforcement Authority confirmed that it had investigated the vessel’s connections to sanctioned entities after the ship entered Finnish waters. The agency determined that Sparta II belonged to a company on the EU sanctions list and imposed a temporary enforcement measure at 8 p.m. Saturday. The measure prohibited the vessel’s release but specifically allowed exceptions when necessary for maritime rescue operations, safety or the reduction of environmental risks. The vessel is operated by Oboronlogistika, a Russian shipping company linked to the country’s Ministry of Defense and involved in transporting military cargo. Ultimately, Finnish authorities allowed the damaged ship to be towed away, citing the risks associated with keeping the vessel in Finnish waters. The rescue operation involved vessels from Finland, Estonia and Russia working together to control the fire and prevent an environmental disaster. According to the Finnish Border Guard , the Russian rescue vessel Murman began towing Sparta II on Sunday, assisted by the Finnish patrol vessel Uisko , the Estonian Navy’s Kindral Kurvits and rescue tugs operated by Alfons Håkans. By Sunday afternoon, thermal imaging showed that some containers aboard the ship remained hot, although flames were no longer visible externally. The vessel was listing slightly but remained stable enough to be towed. Finnish authorities reported no detected leakage of fuel or hazardous substances. The ship subsequently departed Finnish territorial waters and the country’s maritime rescue responsibility area, ending Finland’s direct involvement in the operation. The incident has highlighted growing concerns over the spillover of the Russia-Ukraine war into the Baltic Sea, where attacks against Russian military and logistics assets have increasingly occurred near NATO territory. The Kremlin on Monday accused Ukraine of engaging in what it described as terrorist activity in the Baltic Sea and urged countries in the region to discourage further attacks. articles.title: FedEx-led consortium completes acquisition of InPost
articles.summary: A consortium comprising Advent International, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF Group has completed its acquisition of European parcel delivery company InPost. The transaction, announced on 20 November 2026, brings InPost under private ownership. The company has also been delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Under the new...
articles.body: A consortium comprising Advent International, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF Group has completed its acquisition of European parcel delivery company InPost. The transaction, announced on 20 November 2026, brings InPost under private ownership. The company has also been delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Under the new ownership structure, Advent International and FedEx each hold 37% of the consortium. A&R Investments owns 16%, while PPF Group holds the remaining 10%. InPost will continue operating independently under its existing brand. Its headquarters will remain in Poland, with founder Rafał Brzoska staying on as CEO alongside the current management team. FedEx and InPost target European delivery growth The acquisition brings together FedEx’s global logistics network and InPost’s extensive European parcel delivery infrastructure. InPost operates more than 100,000 out-of-home delivery locations, including over 70,000 automated parcel lockers and close to 30,000 pick-up and drop-off points. The consortium plans to accelerate investment in this network, with further expansion targeted across the United Kingdom, Italy, France, Spain, Portugal and the Benelux region. The investment will also support improvements to InPost’s digital services and customer experience. Meanwhile, FedEx and InPost are exploring opportunities to connect their services more closely. The companies have already entered into separate commercial agreements that allow selected recipients to use InPost’s last-mile delivery services and out-of-home infrastructure in Europe. These arrangements could eventually provide FedEx customers with additional delivery options through InPost’s European network. “Connecting our global network of 3 million businesses and 225 million recipients with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth,” said Raj Subramaniam, President and CEO of FedEx. “We see significant opportunity to expand our commercial arrangements across Europe and look forward to building on it as members of the Consortium,” Subramaniam added. Brzoska said the new ownership structure would provide the capital and expertise needed to support InPost’s continued expansion. The acquisition follows the consortium’s initial agreement, announced in February 2026, to acquire InPost through an all-cash offer of €15.60 per share. With the transaction now completed, InPost will focus on expanding its European delivery network while maintaining its independent operations.

articles.title: MOU Signed to Develop Nuclear-Powered LNG Carrier
articles.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries Co., Ltd. (SHI), Tesser Atomics (Tesser), the Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department of Ocean Operations and Civil Engineering (NTNU), and DNV, have signed a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU),…
articles.body: MOU Signed to Develop Nuclear-Powered LNG Carrier Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © DNV Samsung Heavy Industries Co., Ltd. (SHI), Tesser Atomics (Tesser), the Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department of Ocean Operations and Civil Engineering (NTNU), and DNV, have signed a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), to cooperate on the development of a nuclear-powered LNG carrier demonstration project. The MOU was signed at a collaborative workshop at DNV’s Høvik headquarters in Norway recently. Under the agreement, the project partners will develop a nuclear-powered LNG carrier vessel concept, designed for operation on a route between LNG terminals in the United States and Europe. The first steps of the project involve the partners working together to set out a roadmap that will outline the concept for the demonstration vessel and a plan for safety assessment and approval, all with a view to realizing a practical commercial pathway for the design, construction, and commissioning of the ship. The vessel concept is built around the integration of Tesser’s marinized fluoride-salt-cooled reactor and will serve as a reference for SFI SAINT - Norway’s nuclear-powered vessel research center. The project will be one of multiple demonstration projects conducted in coordination with the NTNU-led SFI SAINT center. The partners bring a range of expertise and experience to drive the project forward. SHI will lead vessel concept development and marine integration, including shipbuilding feasibility and construction methods. Tesser will lead the reactor technology and nuclear plant development, as well as the reactor-specific safety and licensing work. DNV will contribute its expertise in maritime safety, risk assessment and classification, including hazard identification, a safety assessment framework and a classification and verification roadmap. NTNU will coordinate the research, funding proposals and building the project consortium, support feasibility studies, as well as working on simulations, modeling and testing.

articles.title: Indonesia Approves Plan of Development for Geliga Oilfield Six Months After Discovery
articles.summary: Eni announces that the Indonesian authorities have approved the Plan of Development (POD) for the Geliga field (Ganal PSC), a milestone that advances the development of an estimated 8 Tcf of gas in place for both fields of Geliga and Gula in…
articles.body: Indonesia Approves Plan of Development for Geliga Oilfield Six Months After Discovery Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © Eni Eni announces that the Indonesian authorities have approved the Plan of Development (POD) for the Geliga field (Ganal PSC), a milestone that advances the development of an estimated 8 Tcf of gas in place for both fields of Geliga and Gula in the Kutei Basin and consolidates the company's position as a leading gas producer in Indonesia. The approval, granted just six months after the discovery of Geliga, follows the recent start-up of the Maha project and envisages the development of 5.9 Tcf of gas in place and 250 million barrels of associated condensate from the Geliga discovery, together with 2.2 Tcf of gas in place from the existing Gula discovery, for a total of an estimated 8 Tcf of gas in place. Production from the Geliga/Gula hub is expected to peak at 1 Bcf/d of gas and 50,000 barrels of condensate per day. The integrated development of the two fields will create a third production hub in the Kutei Basin, alongside the producing South Hub and the upcoming North Hub, which is currently under execution following the final investment decision (FID) announced earlier this year. With three production hubs in the Kutei Basin, Eni is set to achieve gross production of approximately 3 Bcf/d of gas and 140,000 barrels of condensate per day in East Kalimantan by the end of the decade. This production will serve both domestic and international markets, leveraging synergies with existing facilities in the area, including the Bontang LNG plant and the Jangkrik Floating Production Unit (FPU). The approval of the POD for the Geliga field—now operated by Searah, the independent upstream energy company established through the strategic partnership between Eni and PETRONAS—marks another milestone in the development of Eni's activities in Indonesia's Kutei Basin. The development will comprise 15 subsea wells, flowlines and a newly built FPSO with a processing capacity of approximately 1 Bcf/d of gas and 80,000 barrels of condensate per day, as well as storage capacity of 1,4 million barrels. Gas will be treated onboard the FPSO and transported via pipeline to the onshore receiving facilities at the Santan Terminal and the East Kalimantan gas network. A portion of the gas will be liquefied at the Bontang LNG facility, while the remainder will be supplied to the domestic market through the pipeline network. Condensate will be stabilized and stored onboard the FPSO before being offloaded to shuttle tankers. This new development, together with the ongoing North Hub and Gendalo-Gandang projects, stems from the close strategic partnership with SKK Migas. These projects will have a positive impact on local content development, further increase utilization of the available capacity at the Bontang LNG plant, and provide additional gas supplies for domestic consumption. The new Geliga hub will benefit from synergies with the ongoing execution of the North Hub project, which is expected to start up in 2028. These synergies will contribute to optimizing both costs and execution timelines for the Geliga/Gula development. Eni directly operates the Peri-Mahakam PSC, the Makassar Strait PSC and the recently awarded Sapukala Block. In October 2026, Eni also signed two binding agreements to sell interests in selected Indonesian upstream assets operated by Searah to Pertamina and Medco.

articles.title: France Prepares Major Salvage Operation to Free Grounded Bulk Carrier MIRO G
articles.summary: French authorities are preparing a complex towing operation to free the Malta-flagged bulk carrier MIRO G, which remains stranded on a beach along France’s Atlantic coast after running aground during...
articles.body: Advertise Forum Jobs Subscribe Grab a Seat at the Captain’s Table Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe. Join the leading maritime news network Photo: French Atlantic Maritime Prefecture French authorities are preparing a complex towing operation to free the Malta-flagged bulk carrier MIRO G, which remains stranded on a beach along France’s Atlantic coast after running aground during severe weather last week. In an update Monday, the Atlantic Maritime Prefecture said salvage teams had spent the weekend completing technical assessments and assembling equipment needed for a refloating attempt near Cap de l’Homy, in the Landes department of southwestern France. Central to the operation is a 1,900-meter (6,234-foot) towline being prepared aboard the French emergency towing vessel Abeille Bretagne. The line, transported from the port of La Pallice near La Rochelle, consists of connectable 250-meter sections made from high-strength synthetic fiber. The material is lightweight, buoyant and stronger than steel on an equivalent-weight basis, according to the maritime prefecture. Before attempting to pull the vessel free, salvage teams must restore its ballast pumping capability to remove water and reduce its draft. The work is intended to lighten the ship and improve its chances of being refloated without causing additional damage. Authorities are also watching an improving tidal window. Rising tidal coefficients are expected to provide more than one meter of additional water at high tide compared with conditions on November 19, when the grounding sequence began. The favorable tidal trend is expected to continue through Thursday, November 26. Wind and sea conditions are also improving, although authorities cautioned that conditions remain far from ideal and further strong winds are forecast in the coming days. The MIRO G ran aground during the night of November 19–20 after encountering strong winds and heavy seas off Lit-et-Mixe. The ship had initially anchored approximately three nautical miles offshore before being driven toward the coast. The grounding prompted a coordinated maritime emergency response involving French and Spanish authorities, including deployment of the Spanish salvage tug Sar Gavia and the French tug Abeille Bretagne. Personnel aboard the vessel were subsequently evacuated by helicopter. On Friday, November 20, the French maritime prefect ordered the shipowner to take all necessary measures to arrange the vessel’s refloating as quickly as possible, while ensuring the safety of personnel and protection of the marine environment. Authorities are also preparing pollution-response resources on land and at sea as a precaution against a potential release of fuel or other pollutants during the operation. Despite the improving conditions, officials warned that the longer the ship remains grounded, the greater the risk it will settle deeper into the sand. Even if the initial towing attempt succeeds, an offshore sandbank could create another obstacle as the vessel is moved toward deeper water. The maritime prefecture emphasized that no attempt will proceed until the necessary technical preparations are complete and weather and sea conditions are suitable. The operation remains without a confirmed start date, with authorities seeking to balance the urgency of freeing the vessel against the risks of undertaking a difficult salvage operation in unfavorable conditions. articles.title: $4.4 billion play for ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian oil & gas assets and UK infrastructure expands Vår Energi’s North Sea footprint
articles.summary: Vår Energi is acquiring ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business and related UK infrastructure, strengthening its position as 'Europe’s largest independent E&P company.'
articles.body: Business & Finance November 23, 2026 · 1 hour ago $4.4 billion play for ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian oil & gas assets and UK infrastructure expands Vår Energi’s North Sea footprint Vår Energi is acquiring ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business and related UK infrastructure, strengthening its position as 'Europe’s largest independent E&P company.' MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 3 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Greater Ekofisk Area in the North Sea Source: Vår Energi Norway’s oil and gas company Vår Energi has struck a deal to buy ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian upstream business and related infrastructure interests in the United Kingdom (UK) for an enterprise value of $4.425 billion, in a major deal that will strengthen its position in the North Sea and raise its long-term production target to more than 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boe/d) into the mid-2030s. This acquisition, which includes interests in 13 producing fields, operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area (GEA) and associated export infrastructure, and the Teesside terminal in the UK, is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027 and projected to generate $700 million to $1 billion in post-tax synergies. Together with the previously announced BlueNord combination, the company expects the transaction to further strengthen its position as Europe's largest independent E&P company, positioning it as one of the top three global independent offshore oil and gas producers. Related Articles Fossil Energy Vår Energi-BlueNord merger forging Europe’s new independent oil & gas producer 5 min read The agreed enterprise value of $4.425 billion is based on an economic date of January 1, 2026, while the consideration payable at completion is estimated at around $2.5 billion, net of cash, including cash flow generated by the acquired business from the economic date to completion, as well as customary completion adjustments. The acquisition, expected to close around the end of the first quarter of 2027, is subject to customary conditions, including relevant regulatory and governmental approvals. Vår Energi is also establishing a commodity hedging program for transaction volumes from 2027 through Q1 2028. The firm has secured downside protection for approximately 80% of the additional gas volumes at around $110 per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) while retaining exposure to gas price upside. The acquisition increases the Norwegian player’s long-term production target to above 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day into the mid-2030s. " This is another important step in Vår Energi's growth journey and further strengthens our position on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS). The transaction adds significant scale, reserves and operatorship, while creating the opportunity to unlock materially greater value from a high-quality asset base with substantial remaining resources and development potential. We see significant long-term potential on the NCS. Through the transaction we will continue building on our strong track record of extending the lifetime of fields, which might otherwise have remained underdeveloped. This will contribute to increasing competitiveness and longevity across the NCS, creating further opportunities for industrial development and value creation for all stakeholders and the Norwegian society. " — Nick Walker Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Vår Energi The company will maintain a balanced production mix with around 65% oil and 35% gas after the completion of the transaction and the announced combination with BlueNord, with continued low operating costs of approximately $13 per boe and top quartile emission intensity at approximately 10-11 kg CO2 per boe. " This transaction strengthens our position as the largest independent E&P company in Europe. We are adding a significant portfolio of high-quality and long life assets, providing material cash flow generation and further strengthening our long term financial capacity and flexibility. With available liquidity of USD 7.5 billion and a reduced leverage ratio NIBD/EBITDAX of 0.3x at the end of the third quarter 2026, we can fully fund this transaction through existing liquidity while maintaining our leverage ratio significantly below our target of remaining below 1.3x through the cycles, also benefitting from the material cash generation in 2026 in the acquired business. " — Carlo Santopadre Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Vår Energi According to Vår Energi, the acquisition of ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business and related UK infrastructure brings increased scale, operatorship, recovery potential, and value creation across the asset portfolio, with total reserves and resources to around 2.9 billion boe and reserves and resource life of approximately 14 years. This transaction is expected to deliver $700 million to $1 billion of synergies and additional value creation potential, net present value post-tax, alongside increased free cash flow generation and dividend capacity resulting in boosted dividend guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026 to $450 million. " The Greater Ekofisk Area is a world-class asset with significant remaining resources, extensive infrastructure and decades of production ahead. It remains one of the most important value creation hubs on the NCS. Supported by the highly competent and experienced organisation, which will be fully integrated into Vår Energi, we see substantial opportunities to increase recovery, mature additional resources, and create value over time. The transaction increases our long-term production target to above 500 kboepd into the mid-2030s, reinforcing our position as the Europe's largest independent E&P company and positioning Vår Energi among the world's leading offshore independents, while further strengthening our role as a reliable and secure supplier of energy to Europe. " — Walker added. Vår Energi sees significant opportunities to increase recovery and unlock additional value through an increased operated asset base, field developments, and continued development of resources across the portfolio. The company has strong available liquidity of $7.5 billion as on September 30, 2026. Advertisement " We remain firmly committed to a strong balance sheet and our investment grade credit rating. In consideration of the current volatile price environment, to further de-risk the acquisition we are establishing a commodity hedging programme related to the transaction volumes for 2027 through the first quarter 2028. As of today we have secured downside protection for approximately 80% of the additional gas volumes at approximately USD 110 per boe while retaining exposure to gas price upside. The transaction has an immediate positive effect on our free cash flow and dividend capacity, which is reflected in our increased fourth quarter 2026 dividend guidance of USD 450 million. " — Santopadre emphasized. The acquired portfolio comprises interests in 13 producing fields across the NCS, including the Greater Ekofisk Area, Troll , Heidrun , Alvheim , Oseberg , Visund , Aasta Hansteen , Grane , and Breidablikk , and related infrastructure. Vår Energi describes these assets as being low-cost and carrying limited near-term abandonment liabilities, with a balanced commodity mix and long reserve and resource life based on net 2P reserves of 414 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) and 2C resources of 101 million boe as of year-end 2025. The portfolio is perceived to complement the company’s existing asset base and increase its ownership in several core areas, with around 75% overlap on a combined 2P reserves basis, reflecting the strong strategic fit and existing knowledge of the assets. The transaction adds operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area, including Ekofisk, Eldfisk, Embla, Tor and Tommeliten Alfa and Gamma fields, as well as operatorship of the associated Norpipe pipeline and receiving Teesside facilities in the United Kingdom. Ekofisk was the first commercial discovery on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, and the Greater Ekofisk Area represents one of the largest oil and gas resource bases on the NCS, with initial oil in-place volumes estimated at around 10 billion boe. Vår Energi sees significant opportunities to increase recovery, mature additional resources and extend field life, unlocking long-term value creation. " Through the transaction, we are adding a highly complementary portfolio of long-life assets and a highly experienced and competent team. The increased scale across our operated portfolio creates significant opportunities for further value creation. By applying our value-driven operating model and project factory approach, we see significant potential to increase recovery, enhance performance and deliver substantial synergies across the combined portfolios. We also see opportunities to capture economies of scale across our supply chain and strategic partnerships, infrastructure, logistics and commercial activities. Together, this will strengthen our ability to grow the resource base, increase production and extend the lifetime of our assets in a value-accretive way. articles.title: First well hits target depth offshore Oman as operator gets ready for next one
articles.summary: Masirah Oil has reached target depth at the first well in its drilling campaign offshore Oman and will proceed with the move to the second well.
articles.body: Exploration & Production November 23, 2026 · 1 minute ago First well hits target depth offshore Oman as operator gets ready for next one Masirah Oil has reached target depth at the first well in its drilling campaign offshore Oman and will proceed with the move to the second well. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Block 50 Source: Masirah Oil While Masirah Oil Limited (MOL), an indirect subsidiary of Singapore’s Rex International, is making progress in its drilling campaign off the coast of Oman, the first production has been delayed, with further updates expected as the project progresses. Masirah Oil, which has reached target depth in the drilling of the first well in the current Yumna field campaign, has announced that drilling operations will move forward to the second well in this campaign. However, first production will be delayed and updates will be given as the project progresses, according to the company. articles.body: DHL Global Forwarding has appointed Barbara Eleota as the new CEO of Hillebrand Gori, its specialist beverage logistics business, effective 1 January 2027. Eleota will succeed Dominique von Orelli, who is retiring after more than 40 years with DHL Group. In her new role, she will report directly to Oscar de Bok, CEO of DHL Global Forwarding. She currently serves as Senior Vice President Ocean Freight at DHL Global Forwarding Europe, a position she has held since joining the company in 2024. Eleota brings more than 25 years of logistics experience. She has held senior international freight forwarding positions and has led DHL’s European ocean freight business, focusing on commercial performance and operational development. “Barbara brings extensive international freight forwarding experience, strong commercial expertise and a proven ability to lead organizations across countries and cultures,” said Oscar de Bok, CEO of DHL Global Forwarding. “I am confident that she will build on the strong foundation at Hillebrand Gori and further strengthen the business as a specialist in beverage logistics,” de Bok added. Dominique von Orelli to retire after four decades Von Orelli has served as CEO of Hillebrand Gori since April 2023, following DHL’s acquisition of Hillebrand in March 2022. He began his career with Danzas in 1984 and subsequently held leadership positions across four continents. During his career, he played a significant role in developing DHL Global Forwarding’s ocean freight operations and supporting the acquisition and integration of Hillebrand Gori. His most recent responsibilities included overseeing the company’s integration and organisational transformation. De Bok thanked von Orelli for his contribution and confirmed that he will support Eleota during the leadership transition. Hillebrand Gori will continue operating as DHL Group’s specialist business for beverage logistics under the new leadership arrangement.

MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Island Valiant Source: Mermaid Subsea Services (UK) Aberdeen-headquartered Mermaid Subsea Services (UK) has launched a new framework designed to curb the cost and duration of North Sea decommissioning, with modelling suggesting coordinated campaigns across four operators could enable savings of up to 45% and shorten execution time by 30%. Mermaid Subsea Services has revealed i-DECOM , a campaign framework that coordinates decommissioning across multiple North Sea operators, specifically designed to remove the cost and duplication that come with traditional project-by-project delivery. According to the company, modelling based on a shared campaign across four clients shows i-DECOM could reduce costs by 45% and execution time by 30% compared with standalone projects. " North Sea decommissioning takes more than putting a vessel on contract. It takes experience, technical understanding and the ability to match the right assets and equipment to the specific challenges of each scope. We’ve seen first-hand how poorly matched assets, repeated mobilisation and fragmented delivery drive up cost. So we start with the job: what exactly needs to be delivered, what the right technical solution is, and which assets are best suited to carry it out. Vessel utilisation matters, but it should never come before technical suitability or the client’s commercial interests. " — Scott Cormack Regional Director for Mermaid Subsea Services (UK) Related Articles Vessels North Sea quintet P&A ops done as Mermaid Subsea checks off decom mission 2 min read The UK player explains that decommissioning across the basin has traditionally been planned and contracted one project at a time, which leads to repeated vessel mobilizations, duplicated resources, and operational learning lost between campaigns. In a bid to tackle this, i-DECOM brings the work together, while each operator keeps control of its own scope and decisions, with the framework resting on what the firm describes as a simple principle, where the scope should determine the solution, not the other way round. Rather than planning work around the vessels available, Mermaid defines what each job requires, engineers the technical solution, and then selects the vessel and equipment to deliver it. i-DECOM is led by a specialist late-life team at the company’s Aberdeen facility. This latest development comes as Mermaid marks five years of operations in the North Sea. " i-DECOM applies that thinking at campaign level. By coordinating activity across operators, sharing resources and keeping a dedicated team of specialists together, we can cut unnecessary mobilisation and deliver meaningful savings, while operators keep control of their own scopes. (Source: Atomflot) Cargo volumes along Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) have surpassed 40 million tonnes for the first time, setting a new record for the Arctic shipping corridor. The milestone marks continued growth in Russian Arctic shipping, although volumes remain far below the ambitious targets set forth by President Vladimir Putin over the past decade. Rosatom chief executive Alexey Likhachev said cargo transportation crossed the 40-million-tonne threshold on November 17. The state nuclear corporation, which operates the route’s infrastructure, expects volumes to climb further before the end of the year. The previous record was 37.9 million tonnes in 2024. Traffic slipped to 37.02 million tonnes in 2025 , but the latest milestone puts the NSR back on an upward trajectory. Over the past five years, annual cargo volumes have increased from 34.87 million tonnes in 2021 to more than 40 million tonnes in 2026, an increase of roughly 15%. The route carried 34.07 million tonnes in 2022 and 36.25 million tonnes in 2023 before reaching its previous peak in 2024. The figures underline the NSR’s growing importance to Russia’s Arctic economy, but also show that recent growth has been relatively modest compared with the rapid expansion earlier in the decade. The latest record remains a long way from Moscow’s original ambitions. Putin set a target of 80 million tonnes of annual cargo traffic by 2024 in a 2018 presidential decree. Actual shipments that year reached less than half that volume. Even with this year’s record, the route is still operating at around half the level the Kremlin had targeted two years ago. Transit shipping, however, has shown stronger growth this year. Unlike total NSR cargo figures, which include shipments to and from Russian Arctic ports and resource projects, transit cargo refers to goods passing through the route between destinations outside the region connecting Europe and Asia. Transit volumes reached 6 million tonnes by early November, twice the level recorded during the same period last year, according to Russian Arctic Development Minister Alexey Chekunkov. Rosatom official Vladimir Panov has forecast that full-year transit traffic could exceed 7 million tonnes, which would more than double the 3.2 million tonnes recorded in 2025 . Independent tracking offers a more cautious picture. The Centre for High North Logistics estimated that transit cargo totaled approximately 3.7 million tonnes by the end of September, with the season potentially exceeding 4.5 million tonnes if ongoing voyages were completed . The final figures will help clarify how much of the Russian forecast materializes. The overall growth in NSR traffic remains heavily dependent on Russian energy exports, particularly liquefied natural gas, crude oil and petroleum products. Yamal LNG has been a major contributor, while new shipments from Rosneft’s Vostok Oil project could add further volumes in the coming years as its Arctic infrastructure develops. articles.summary: An Iranian oil tanker with no track record signaled earlier on Monday that it had sailed past a US blockade outside the Strait of Hormuz — an unlikely trajectory that is raising fresh questions about obfuscation tactics and analysts’ limited ability to accurately track movements in the area.

REUTERS/Amr Alfiky By Weilun Soon Nov 23, 2026 (Bloomberg) –An Iranian oil tanker with no track record signaled earlier on Monday that it had sailed past a US blockade outside the Strait of Hormuz — an unlikely trajectory that is raising fresh questions about obfuscation tactics and analysts’ limited ability to accurately track movements in the area. A vessel purporting to be the Khat Shekan, an Iranian very large crude carrier, appeared on Sunday on some ship-tracking platforms including MarineTraffic, indicating it was beginning an exit from the Persian Gulf. By Monday, signals suggested it had made it past US forces — a first since the blockade was reimposed in July. The catch is that the position is very likely fake and the ship — whose name translates as “Line Breaker” — may not exist at all, according to analysts and maritime tracking experts. Tehran may instead be sending a message on what it can still do to tangle the global oil trade after nine months of conflict with the US, by making already challenging monitoring efforts even more difficult, they said. “Any attempts to complicate the monitoring of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz are an unwelcome addition to an already dangerous situation,” said Mark Douglas, an analyst at ship-tracking platform Starboard Maritime Intelligence. The signals suggest the vessel is a laden crude tanker heading for China’s Zhoushan port, but it has no International Maritime Organization number, a unique identifier for vessels that remains through their operational life. A search done on its maritime mobile service identity, or MMSI number on the IMO database, yields no results, with an error message stating: “Only ships in service are displayed.” There is also no record of voyages prior to Sunday, and the vessel does not appear on Bloomberg or other ship-tracking and intelligence platforms, including Starboard, Kpler, Vortexa and Equasis. “Our analysis indicates AIS spoofing,” MarineTraffic wrote in a social media post , referring to the practice of sending false tracking or navigation data to plant incorrect information or confuse observers. Ship operators engaged in so-called “dark” trades have long sought to misrepresent vessels’ identities and locations in order to mask their journeys and the cargoes they are handling. Tankers ferrying US-sanctioned Iranian oil before the war often spoofed their positions, or assumed the identities of demolished ships. Iran all but closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to US attacks, but its crude exports continued in the first months of the conflict. The reintroduction of a US naval blockade, however, severed a vital financial lifeline for Tehran at a time when others in the Persian Gulf are using dark shuttles and other workarounds to restore pre-war flows. Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The country has repeatedly vowed to break the blockade, however. On Saturday, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the country would take “whatever measures are necessary” to do so. By Lina Golovnya Nov 23 (Reuters) – Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using naval drones on Sunday , the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Zelenskiy said on Monday morning that Ukraine used seven naval drones in Sunday’s attack, and had also hit the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara , which he said Russia had used to transport weapons. “Despite all the enemy’s attempts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette ‘ Mercury ‘ was sunk,” Zelenskiy posted on Telegram, the first official acknowledgement that Ukraine has carried out an attack in Libya. “We continue operations in designated waters.” Zelenskiy said a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter had been destroyed along with the corvette. Russia’s Defence Ministry did not immediately comment. EASTERN LIBYA HAS MILITARY TIES TO RUSSIA After a civil war, eastern Libya is controlled by military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose Libyan National Army has ties with Russia, while the west is controlled by an internationally recognized Government of National Unity based in Tripoli. Libya’s eastern-based government said the corvette was docked at the Benghazi naval base on Sunday when it was hit. The Institute for the Study of War said it had stopped for several days, under a cooperation agreement, to refuel and resupply as it escorted Russian cargo ships that can carry military suppliesheading for Russia. Osama Hamad, prime minister of Libya’s eastern-based government, said he had asked the UN to investigate “suspicions that the boats had been launched from western Libya” and to verify the presence of Ukrainian military experts there. No comment was immediately available from the Tripoli government. Russia’s Transport Ministry said in March that Ukrainian naval drones launched from Libya had attacked the Arctic Metagaz, which was carrying liquefied natural gas from Murmansk. Libya’s maritime agency reported that the vessel had sunk between Libya and Malta after catching fire. Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for that attack. GULF OF FINLAND DRONE ATTACK ON RUSSIAN SHIP On Saturday , a drone attack set fire to another Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, operated by the Russian defense logistics firm Oboronlogistika, in international waters in the Gulf of Finland. The Finnish military said it was likely to have been carried out by Ukraine, although Kyiv did not immediately comment. All 16 crew were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship, one of them slightly injured. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov responded to a question about the attack by saying there was a “dangerous trend of increasing terrorist activity” in the Baltic Sea. He said Moscow hoped states in the area would warn Kyiv off such operations. Russian, Estonian and Finnish vessels fought the fire after the Sparta II drifted into Finnish waters, and a Russian ship began towing it away on Sunday. US-backed talks between Russia and Ukraine resumed this month after a nine-month hiatus in an effort to end the war, Europe’s biggest since World War Two, albeit with little result so far. Mykola Bielieskov of the National Institute for Strategic Studies in Kyiv said Ukraine was looking to strengthen its position with “horizontal escalation.” “Since neither side is able to compel the other to accept terms of settlement through the battlefield only, both try to find new ways to pressure each other,” he said. articles.body: Asia Dry Cargo Precious Shipping secures year-long ultramax charter Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 161 1 minute read Precious Shipping Precious Shipping Thailand’s Precious Shipping has secured another index-linked ultramax charter with Singapore’s PACC Line, fixing the 2015-built Sarita Naree for up to 13 months at a current equivalent rate of around $23,700 per day. The Khalid Hashim-led owner said the 62,964 dwt vessel started an 11-to-13-month charter on November 22 at a gross variable rate equivalent to 103% of the Baltic Exchange Supramax Index (BSI-63K) weighted time-charter average over the preceding 15 days. The hire will fluctuate with the index rather than remain fixed at the current level. The latest agreement follows a similar fixture in September, when Precious chartered its 2016-built ultramax Sunisa Naree to PACC Line for 11 to 13 months at the same 103% index-linked rate, then equivalent to about $23,000 per day. Both vessels were built at China’s Taizhou Sanfu Ship Engineering, a yard that has become central to Precious Shipping’s fleet renewal programme. PACC Line, part of the Kuok Maritime Group through Pacific Carriers, operates a fleet of around 50 vessels across dry bulk, breakbulk and project cargo trades. The latest fixing adds to a string of longer-term employment deals for Precious. In October, the company chartered its recently delivered Rossarin Naree to Oman’s Asyad Shipping for 12 to 14 months at 108% of the same index, then equivalent to about $24,000 per day. Precious has also continued investing in larger bulkers, returning to Sanfu in September for four 64,500 dwt ultramaxes worth $141.8m, with deliveries scheduled between April 2030 and January 2031. The Japanese utility signed a share purchase agreement with Ocean Winds on November 19, and the transaction will be carried out through...
articles.body: Asia Europe Offshore Renewables Kansai Electric takes 40% stake in Polish offshore wind project Bojan Lepic November 23, 2026 0 115 1 minute read Ocean Winds Ocean Winds Japan’s Kansai Electric Power has agreed to acquire a 40% interest in Ocean Winds’ 390 MW BC-Wind offshore wind development in Poland, marking its first investment in the country. The Japanese utility signed a share purchase agreement with Ocean Winds on November 19, and the transaction will be carried out through its wholly owned subsidiary, KPIC Netherlands. Kansai will acquire its interest in C-Wind Polska, the project company developing the wind farm, leaving Ocean Winds with a 60% holding following completion. BC-Wind is located approximately 23 km off Poland’s Baltic Sea coast and will comprise 26 Siemens Gamesa turbines with a maximum output of 15 MW each. The project is expected to start generating electricity in 2028 and can supply around 500,000 Polish households. Ocean Winds, a joint venture between EDP Renewables and Engie, reached financial close on BC-Wind in December 2025, securing approximately €2bn ($2.2bn) in project financing. Offshore construction is advancing, with foundation installation scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. Belgian contractor DEME has secured the foundation and subsea cable installation work, while Seaway 7 is responsible for installing the transition piece and offshore substation. Cadeler will handle the transportation and installation of the 26 turbines in 2028. Kansai said the acquisition would increase the attributable capacity of its overseas power generation portfolio to approximately 2.65 GW once completed. The deal expands Japanese investment in Poland’s offshore wind sector as the country moves ahead with its first generation of large-scale Baltic Sea projects.
