articles.title: €2.8 billion UK-Germany energy link continues to take shape as nearshore cabling works begin on German coast
articles.summary: Prysmian has started laying 30 kilometers of nearshore cabling at Wilhelmshaven, advancing the 725-kilometer UK-Germany electricity interconnector.
articles.body: Business Developments & Projects November 23, 2026 · 29 minutes ago €2.8 billion UK-Germany energy link continues to take shape as nearshore cabling works begin on German coast Prysmian has started laying 30 kilometers of nearshore cabling at Wilhelmshaven, advancing the 725-kilometer UK-Germany electricity interconnector. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Prysmian's Ulisse cable laying vessel Source: NeuConnect A new milestone in bringing the first direct electricity connection between the United Kingdom (UK) and Germany closer to reality has been reached, with cable installation works advancing along Germany’s northern coast near Wilhelmshaven. A cable-laying vessel operated by Italy’s Prysmian has embarked on the installation of 30 kilometers of nearshore cabling, marking further progress in establishing the electricity link between the two countries. Prysmian’s Ulisse cable laying vessel has begun laying 30 kilometers of cabling at the German shore in Wilhelmshaven for NeuConnect , described as the first direct energy link between the UK and Germany, following the continued progress of the wider 700-kilometer subsea cabling program, which passed the halfway stage earlier this year. The Italian contractor kicked off NeuConnect ’s subsea cabling works at the end of 2024, with all cabling completed in UK waters earlier this year and now continuing in German waters. Alongside this, cable landing works have started at the German end of the cabling route, including the Ulisse vessel’s laying of 30 kilometers of cabling in the near shore area in northern Germany. Upon completion of cable landing works, the offshore cable will reach the mainland at Hooksiel, where a 12-kilometer onshore section of cabling is in place to connect into NeuConnect’s new converter station currently under construction near Wilhelmshaven. Prysmian has now put well over 350 kilometers of offshore and onshore cabling in place across the project’s wider subsea cabling program. Related Articles Interconnectors Fit-out of NeuConnect’s converter stations in progress 2 min read " With our subsea cabling program well over the halfway point, the start of cable landing works in Germany marks another important milestone. At both ends of the project, we can see this vital new UK-German energy link continue to take shape, and we remain firmly on track. " — Arnaud Grévoz Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NeuConnect This £2.4 billion - €2.8 billion UK-Germany electricity link is led by Meridiam , Allianz , Kansai Electric Power , and TEPCO . NeuConnect is expected to be one of the world’s largest interconnectors with around 725 kilometers of land and subsea cables forming an invisible energy highway to connect two of Europe’s largest energy markets for the first time. The new connection will allow 1.4 GW of electricity to flow in either direction, which is estimated to be enough to power up to 1.5 million homes, landing a hand in boosting energy security while also helping to integrate renewable energy sources in the UK and Germany. articles.summary: Hong Kong-based dry bulk owner Jinhui Shipping and Transportation has found a new buyer for its 2012-built supramax Jin Bi, securing $17.8m for a vessel it unsuccessfully tried to sell for $14.4m earlier this year. articles.body: Dry Cargo Greater China Jinhui finds new buyer for supramax at higher price Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 268 1 minute read Jinhui Holdings Jinhui Holdings Hong Kong-based dry bulk owner Jinhui Shipping and Transportation has found a new buyer for its 2012-built supramax Jin Bi , securing $17.8m for a vessel it unsuccessfully tried to sell for $14.4m earlier this year. The Oslo-listed company has signed a memorandum of agreement with Singapore-based Global Pacific Shipping for the 56,361 dwt bulker, with delivery scheduled between November 25 and December 30. The deal marks a second attempt to sell the ship after a previous agreement with Hong Kong’s Xing Le Investments collapsed in January. Jinhui had agreed to sell Jin Bi for $14.4m in December 2025, but the transaction was cancelled the following month after a contractual condition relating to timely delivery could not be met. The latest agreement puts another $3.4m on the price tag and comes with improved payment terms. Unlike the previous arrangement, which included $7m payable over four years, Global Pacific will pay the full purchase price before delivery. Jinhui said it expects to book a gain of approximately $5.2m on the sale, based on the vessel’s carrying value of $12.6m at the end of September. Proceeds will be used primarily to repay short-term borrowings, settle outstanding liabilities and strengthen liquidity. The disposal adds to Jinhui’s ongoing fleet reshuffle. Last month, the company agreed to sell the 2007-built, 55,496 dwt Jin Xing for $14.6m, continuing its clearout of older supramax tonnage. At the same time, the Ng family-controlled owner has been investing heavily in larger bulk carriers, with 14 ultramax newbuildings lined up at Chinese yards, including Jiangmen Nanyang, New Dayang and Jiangsu Hantong. Jinhui currently operates 19 bulk carriers, comprising 16 owned vessels and three chartered-in ships, ahead of the latest disposal. articles.title: BIMCO-initiated proposal for an ISO methodology on shipbuilding emissions enters the ISO process
articles.summary: A proposed ISO Technical Specification would set a common way to calculate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from building a ship. We invite experts to help shape it through their national standards body. A proposal for a new ISO project has been submitted to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The...
articles.body: BIMCO-initiated proposal for an ISO methodology on shipbuilding emissions enters the ISO process in International Shipping News 23/11/2026 A proposed ISO Technical Specification would set a common way to calculate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from building a ship. We invite experts to help shape it through their national standards body. A proposal for a new ISO project has been submitted to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The project would develop a common methodology for calculating GHG emissions from shipbuilding. It covers the emissions a ship generates before it enters service, from raw material extraction to shipyard construction and sea trial. The proposal started as a BIMCO initiative and was developed by a BIMCO-led industry working group. Danish Standards formally submitted it on 4 October 2026. Participating national standards bodies are now voting on it, and the ballot closes on 27 December 2026. If the proposal is approved, Everllence and Danish Standards will lead further development, with support from BIMCO. Closing a gap in lifecycle emissions data The shipping industry has traditionally focused on emissions from burning fuel during ship operations. Existing mandatory IMO regulations already cover these emissions, including IMO fuel consumption reporting and the IMO Guidelines on life cycle GHG intensity of marine fuels. However, a ship also generates substantial emissions before it enters service. Sources include raw material extraction, steel and other materials, component manufacturing, transport and shipyard work. There is currently no harmonised, shipping-specific methodology for calculating these emissions. “We initiated this work because the lack of a common methodology creates a gap for shipowners seeking reliable information about the lifecycle GHG emissions of their assets. By bringing together parties from across the maritime value chain, we have developed a concrete technical proposal that has now entered the formal ISO process,” Aron Frank Sørensen, BIMCO’s Chief Environment Officer The methodology would be relevant for shipowners who: • Choose to report Scope 3 GHG emissions voluntarily, such as emissions from buying newbuild ships, using frameworks like the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard • Are required to calculate and report Scope 3 emissions under regional or national legislation. From raw materials to sea trials The proposed Technical Specification covers cradle-to-gate emissions. This runs from the extraction and processing of raw materials through: • Component manufacturing and transport • Shipyard construction • Waste handling • Launching, testing and sea trials. Equipment manufacturers, repair yards and shipowners could also apply the same methodology to major conversions, major repairs and new equipment installed during a ship’s operational lifetime. Some emissions are outside the proposed scope: fuel use during operation, day-to-day maintenance after delivery, and anything after a ship arrives for recycling. Existing regulations and standards cover some of these emissions, and future ISO standards could cover other lifecycle emissions. “We need a standardised approach to calculating GHG emissions from shipbuilding to be able to focus on emissions arising from this part of the maritime industry. Through an international, technical standard we can achieve a harmonised way of identifying hotspots in the construction process and recognise the role of shipbuilding in the overall emissions calculation,” Edith Buhl, Life Cycle Assessment Specialist at Everllence Denmark A/S and nominated project leader for the ISO project proposal. Practical calculation options The proposed methodology builds on the ISO 14040 and ISO 14060 families of standards and the GHG Protocol. It offers four calculation methods to suit different levels of available data: • Supplier-specific • Hybrid • Average-data • Spend-based. Supplier-specific data would be preferred where it is available. The other methods would allow credible estimates where detailed data is not yet accessible. Greater transparency between buyer and builder A harmonised methodology could help shipowners, shipyards, equipment manufacturers and other stakeholders calculate, disclose and ultimately reduce shipbuilding emissions. It could also help identify emissions hotspots, support credible sustainability reporting and reduce the risk of inconsistent or misleading GHG reduction claims. The methodology is meant to make it clearer to both parties which calculation methods were used: the shipowner as buyer and the shipyard as seller. It could also make reliable emissions data easier and cheaper for shipowners to obtain, because shipyards could follow a methodology set by ISO instead of developing their own. Results will not automatically be comparable between ships or companies. Comparability will depend on consistent boundaries, calculation methods, data quality and disclosed assumptions. BIMCO’s aim is not to set a particular environmental performance level, but rather to aim for a credible, practical methodology so the industry can calculate and report emissions on a consistent basis. From Tripartite to ISO The project started in the Tripartite forum, which brings together shipyards, international shipowners’ organisations and IACS classification societies. • November 2024: Tripartite agreed that a joint industry working group, led by BIMCO, should prepare input for a possible ISO project on GHG accounting for shipbuilding • May to December 2025: BIMCO chaired the working group. Its roughly 20 participants represented shipowner associations, shipowners, shipbuilding associations, shipyards, equipment manufacturers and classification societies. The group produced the initial draft methodology that accompanies the proposal • June 2026: After working with Danish Standards to bring the proposal into the ISO process, BIMCO presented it in Paris to ISO/TC 8/SC 25 on Maritime GHG Reduction. Discussions there indicated strong support. A starting point, not a finished standard The industry draft is intentionally a starting point for ISO’s technical work, not the final methodology. The ISO working group can reconsider everything in it, and the participating experts still have significant technical work to do. The proposal is for a Technical Specification rather than an International Standard because the methodology needs further technical development and practical industry input. Depending on how it works in practice, it could later become the basis for an International Standard. If the proposal is approved, work is expected to start in January 2027 under ISO/TC 8/SC 25/WG 3 (Maritime GHG assessment and documentation). The proposed development period is 24 months, with completion by December 2028. “The project comes at an important time, when the industry needs a common language for greenhouse gas emissions. Standards are strongest when they are built on industry expertise and practical experience. That is why it is important for industry stakeholders to engage through their national standards bodies and contribute to developing the common solutions the industry will need,” Asker Juul, Head of Energy and Transport at Danish Standards. Call for experts The methodology needs active participation from shipbuilders, equipment manufacturers, shipowners and other stakeholders to be technically sound and workable across the global maritime value chain. Participation from the major shipbuilding, ship-owning and equipment-manufacturing nations is especially important. That will help make sure the methodology works across regions, jurisdictions and corporate GHG accounting frameworks. We invite Interested experts to contribute their knowledge and perspectives and help shape the new specification. Both technical expertise and a practical, user-oriented perspective are important to ensure that the specification is robust and applicable in practice. By taking part, experts will also gain early insight into its development and final direction. Participation takes place through their national standards body. Source: BIMCO, https://www.bimco.org/news-insights/bimco-news/2026/11/18-iso/ 2026-11-23 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: LNG Market Remained Under Pressure Last Week, As LPGs Firmed
articles.summary: The LNG market remained under pressure this week, with an abundance of prompt vessel availability in the Atlantic continuing to weigh on freight rates. articles.body: LNG Market Remained Under Pressure Last Week, As LPGs Firmed in International Shipping News 23/11/2026 The LNG market remained under pressure this week, with an abundance of prompt vessel availability in the Atlantic continuing to weigh on freight rates. Increased fixing activity and firmer requirements offered little support to rates, as ample tonnage allowed charterers to maintain aggressive bids. On the BLNG1 Gladstone–Tokyo route, rates declined $2,800 week-on-week to settle at $50,600/day. Pacific rates remained comparatively supported to the West. The BLNG2 Sabine–Isle of Grain route fell $8,900 to settle at $20,800/day, with the Atlantic remaining considerably oversupplied amid limited arbitrage opportunities and increased FOB cargo sales. Similarly, the BLNG3 Sabine–Tokyo route declined $15,200 to close at $40,400/day, reflecting the continued weakness in the Atlantic and reduced demand for longer-haul voyages. Period rates also softened, with the six-month assessment falling $1,900 to $42,300/day, the one-year assessment down $2,267 to $50,633/day, and the three-year assessment easing $700 to $70,300/day. LPG The LPG market firmed this week, with a notable pick-up in activity in the US Gulf. Close to around 10 cargoes were fixed or worked for the upcoming month, steadily absorbing available tonnage and tightening the position list. On the BLPG1 Ras Tanura–Chiba route, rates settled at $252.40/tonne, with TCE earnings closing at $246,826/day. The BLPG2 Houston–Flushing route softened marginally, declining $0.67 week-on-week to settle at $173.83/tonne, with TCE earnings down $479 to $204,608/day. Similarly, the BLPG3 Houston–Chiba route eased $0.43 to close at $310.43/tonne, while TCE returns fell $427 to settle at $189,690/day. Despite the slight decline, sentiment in the US Gulf has strengthened, with further activity expected. Source: Baltic Exchange 2026-11-23 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: GXO to expand warehouse automation across US operations in 2027
articles.summary: GXO Logistics plans to accelerate the deployment of automation technologies across its US operations, with the rollout scheduled to begin in early 2027. The company will introduce a range of robotic and AI-powered systems at selected facilities over the following 12 months. The initiative will support customers in...
articles.body: GXO Logistics plans to accelerate the deployment of automation technologies across its US operations, with the rollout scheduled to begin in early 2027. The company will introduce a range of robotic and AI-powered systems at selected facilities over the following 12 months. The initiative will support customers in several industries, including retail, consumer goods, food and beverage, aerospace, defence and technology. According to GXO, the new systems aim to improve warehouse productivity, inventory accuracy and workplace safety. New technologies to support warehouse operations The planned rollout includes autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) designed to transport pallets and reduce repetitive manual handling. GXO will also introduce robotic arms for activities such as unloading and packing, alongside automated sorting systems. Other technologies include AI-enabled vision systems and wearable scanning devices. These tools will support hands-free data collection and more efficient inventory checks. The company said the systems are designed to fit into existing warehouse operations with limited disruption. “Today’s supply chains require solutions that are efficient and adaptable,” said Michael Jacobs, CEO of the Americas & Asia Pacific, GXO. “This deployment underscores our commitment to helping customers modernize their operations with technologies that can deliver immediate value while positioning them for long-term growth,” Jacobs added. The initiative reflects GXO’s broader investment in warehouse automation as customers seek more flexible and efficient logistics operations. The company expects the technologies to help optimise labour resources and improve service levels across participating sites. GXO has not disclosed the number of facilities included in the rollout, the planned number of robots or the associated investment. The deployment remains scheduled for 2027, with operational results to be assessed as the systems are introduced.

articles.body: Middle East Offshore Arabian Drilling picks up $400m in long-term offshore work Bojan Lepic November 23, 2026 0 375 1 minute read Arabian Drilling Arabian Drilling Saudi Arabian drilling contractor Arabian Drilling has secured a SAR1.5bn ($400m) long-term contract from Khafji Joint Operations (KJO) to provide and operate two self-propelled offshore service units. The agreement replaces existing contracts covering two offshore service units operating for KJO. The first unit will operate under a 10-year contract, with work expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026. The second has secured a 15-year agreement, with operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2028. Arabian Drilling said the agreements represent the longest offshore service unit contracts in its history and will provide additional long-term revenue visibility. The latest award takes the company’s cumulative contracted backlog to approximately SAR18.5bn ($4.9bn), a record for the Saudi contractor. Khafji Joint Operations is a joint venture between Aramco Gulf Operations and Kuwait Gulf Oil, responsible for oil and gas production in the Saudi–Kuwaiti Divided Zone. The contract follows Arabian Drilling’s September award of four high-specification offshore jackup contracts from KJO, worth approximately SAR2bn ($533m). Those four-year drilling contracts are expected to contribute to revenue from the final quarter of 2026. Arabian Drilling said the latest agreement maintains its entire share of KJO’s offshore service unit segment. The company did not disclose the names of the two units or the individual contract values. articles.summary: State-owned Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) is pressing ahead with a fleet expansion drive worth an estimated $3.2bn, launching tenders for up to 22 newbuildings across the gas carrier, tanker and container segments, alongside a separate push for secondhand tonnage. articles.body: Asia Containers Gas Tankers Shipping Corp of India casts $3.2bn net for 22 ships Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 760 2 minutes read SCI SCI State-owned Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) is pressing ahead with a fleet expansion drive worth an estimated $3.2bn, launching tenders for up to 22 newbuildings across the gas carrier, tanker and container segments, alongside a separate push for secondhand tonnage. The Mumbai-listed owner has issued tenders covering eight 88,000 cu m very large gas carriers (VLGCs), six 18,000 teu containerships, up to six 8,000 teu boxships and two 155,000 dwt suezmax tankers. The largest package involves eight VLGCs, with bids due by January 27, 2027, and an estimated combined value of $950m. The vessels are being sought for a proposed joint venture involving state-owned energy companies Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum. The gas carrier programme comes with a significant domestic construction requirement. Two vessels are to be built at an established overseas yard, with the remaining six earmarked for construction in India under arrangements involving qualified international shipbuilders. SCI is taking a similar approach to its six 18,000 teu containerships. Two vessels are intended for its own fleet, while four are earmarked for the proposed Bharat Container Shipping Line, part of India’s efforts to expand its presence in international container shipping. The tender again splits construction between two ships overseas and four in India, with bids due by December 10.The company is also pursuing six LNG-ready containerships of 8,000 teu, comprising two firm vessels and four options, in a programme previously valued at around $720m. That tender, first launched in July, has since been revised to require two vessels to be constructed overseas and four in India if the full package proceeds. Bids are now due by December 7. In the tanker segment, SCI has opened bidding for two 155,000 dwt suezmax crude carriers, with offers due by December 10. The owner is also looking to the secondhand market to bolster its container fleet. A separate tender seeks two firm and two optional boxships of between 1,500 teu and 2,500 teu, with vessels up to 20 years old eligible. The deadline for offers is December 17. The latest procurement drive represents a major expansion of SCI’s fleet renewal ambitions, with the government using state-backed orders to attract foreign shipbuilding expertise and move more complex vessel construction to Indian yards. SCI currently operates a fleet of 58 vessels across the tanker, dry bulk, container and offshore sectors, according to its latest published fleet figures. Just two are owned containerships. None of the newbuilding packages has yet been announced as a firm shipbuilding contract. The $3.2bn figure represents an industry estimate of the proposed programme, which includes optional tonnage. articles.summary: US energy major ExxonMobil and its partners have taken a final investment decision worth an estimated $4bn to redevelop the Kizomba A and B fields offshore Angola, while announcing a fresh hydrocarbon discovery in the same block. articles.body: Africa Americas Offshore ExxonMobil greenlights $4bn Angola offshore redevelopment Bojan Lepic November 23, 2026 0 502 1 minute read ExxonMobil ExxonMobil US energy major ExxonMobil and its partners have taken a final investment decision worth an estimated $4bn to redevelop the Kizomba A and B fields offshore Angola, while announcing a fresh hydrocarbon discovery in the same block. The investment decision, formalised on November 19, completes the approvals for the Block 15 Life Extension Project, following the sanctioning of the Kizomba C redevelopment last year. The programme will make use of existing offshore infrastructure to develop additional resources across the Kizomba production hub, located around 145 km off Angola’s northern coast. The investment also includes plans to develop the Likembe field, with ExxonMobil looking to extend production from one of Angola’s most prolific deepwater areas. The Block 15 production-sharing agreement was previously extended until 2037, giving the partners more time to develop remaining resources. Meanwhile, Angola’s National Oil, Gas and Biofuels Agency (ANPG) confirmed a new discovery at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 exploration well, approximately 350 km northwest of Luanda. The Valaris DS-9 drillship drilled the well in about 1,400 m of water and encountered 65.4 m of hydrocarbon-bearing sandstone with good reservoir characteristics. The discovery is the 21st recorded in Block 15 and the second this year. No recoverable resource estimate has been disclosed. ExxonMobil operates Block 15 with a 36% stake, alongside Azule Energy entities holding a combined 42%, Equinor with 12%, and Sonangol with 10%. The latest investment and exploration success comes as Angola seeks to sustain offshore production by redeveloping mature fields and pursuing further deepwater exploration. articles.body: Europe Greater China Shipyards Tankers Aegean Shipping adds fresh tanker pair at COSCO yard Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 346 1 minute read Aegean Shipping Aegean Shipping George Melissanidis-led Aegean Shipping Management has been linked to another two LR2 tanker newbuildings at COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry’s Yangzhou yard in China, extending its tanker investment programme into 2030. Greek shipping sources have identified the latest pair as ice class 1C product tankers scheduled for delivery in the first quarter of 2030. No contract price has emerged. The fresh deal would take the Piraeus-based owner’s tanker orderbook to nine ships, comprising seven LR2s and two VLCCs. The move builds on Aegean’s long-running relationship with COSCO, where the company has commissioned a series of tankers and bulk carriers over more than a decade. Including the latest pair, Aegean’s cumulative newbuilding programme with the Chinese shipbuilding group would reach 18 vessels. The company has also been expanding its ties with Hengli Heavy Industries. Earlier this year, Aegean made its first move into the VLCC sector through a newbuilding agreement at the Dalian-based shipbuilder. That programme was subsequently reshaped and expanded to include three LR2 tankers and two VLCCs, following the exercise of an option for a second supertanker in September. Aegean has meanwhile been taking advantage of strong secondhand tanker values to reshape its fleet. The owner sold the 2022-built, 114,319 dwt Green Adventure for around $83m in September, following the disposal of the 2018-built aframax Green Attitude for a reported $71m earlier in the year.
